units.title: Vectors: arrows made of numbers
units.summary: A point in space is a list of numbers, and a vector is an arrow you can add to another or stretch.

units.title: Distance between two points
units.summary: The straight-line distance between two points comes from Pythagoras' theorem, in 2D or 3D.

units.title: Multiplying a matrix by a vector
units.summary: A matrix is a table of numbers that turns one vector into another through weighted sums.

units.title: Rotating points with a matrix
units.summary: A rotation matrix turns every point of a shape by the same angle without changing its size.

units.title: The derivative: slope at a point
units.summary: The derivative measures how fast a quantity changes: the slope of its graph at one point.

units.title: The gradient: the uphill direction
units.summary: The gradient collects one slope per input into a vector that points uphill fastest.

units.title: Random draws: chance you can repeat
units.summary: A random draw picks a value by chance, and a seed makes a computer's random choices repeatable.

units.title: The bell curve (normal distribution)
units.summary: The normal distribution describes values that cluster around an average and thin out evenly on both sides.

units.title: Summarizing a list of numbers
units.summary: The mean gives a list's typical value, and the standard deviation its typical distance from that value.

units.title: Normalizing data
units.summary: Normalizing shifts data to center on zero and rescales it, so different examples share one size.

units.title: Sine waves
units.summary: Sine and cosine turn an angle or a position into a smooth wave that repeats.

units.title: Exponentials, undone by logarithms
units.summary: An exponential grows by repeated multiplication, and the logarithm counts the multiplications back.

units.title: Graphs: dots joined by lines
units.summary: A graph is a set of things, called nodes, with links, called edges, between some pairs of them.

units.title: Connected pieces of a graph
units.summary: A connected component is a group of nodes you can travel between along edges; cutting an edge can split it in two.

units.title: Reading Python for this course
units.summary: Just enough Python to read the code here (variables, lists, loops, functions), with pointers to full courses.

units.title: Arrays in NumPy
units.summary: A NumPy array holds many numbers in a grid with a shape, so one line of code can work on all of them at once.

units.title: PyTorch tensors on the GPU
units.summary: A PyTorch tensor is an array that can live on a graphics card, where thousands of numbers are processed at once.

units.title: Automatic gradients in PyTorch
units.summary: PyTorch records the operations that produced a number and works backward to find how each input changes it.

units.title: Nearest-neighbor search
units.summary: Finding the closest point to a query by checking every point works, but it slows down as the points multiply.

units.title: KD-trees: nearest neighbors fast
units.summary: A KD-tree splits space into boxes, so a search can skip every box that cannot hold a closer point.

units.title: Farthest-point sampling
units.summary: Farthest-point sampling covers a shape evenly with a few points, always taking the point whose nearest picked point is farthest away.

units.title: Matching two sets: the assignment problem
units.summary: The assignment problem pairs each item of one set with one item of another so that the total cost is as small as possible.

units.title: Shapes as point clouds
units.summary: A point cloud describes a shape by many points on or inside it, in no particular order.

units.title: 3D images made of voxels
units.summary: A 3D image is a grid of tiny boxes called voxels, which need not be the same size along every axis.

units.title: Segmentation: a label for every voxel
units.summary: Segmentation gives every voxel a label number that says which object it belongs to.

units.title: Supervoxels: small pieces to merge
units.summary: Supervoxels are small, confident pieces of a segmentation that are later joined into whole objects.

units.title: Connectomics: mapping neurons from images
units.summary: Connectomics reconstructs neurons and their connections from electron-microscope images.

units.title: Two kinds of segmentation error
units.summary: A merge error joins two objects under one label, and a split error cuts one object into several.

units.title: Proofreading a segmentation
units.summary: Proofreading finds and fixes merge and split errors, by hand or with software that proposes fixes.

units.title: Data augmentation: new views of an example
units.summary: Data augmentation trains on randomly rotated or jittered copies of each example, so a model learns what should not matter.

units.title: A linear layer: weighted sums
units.summary: A linear layer turns an input vector into an output vector through weighted sums whose weights are learned.

units.title: Activation functions: bending straight lines
units.summary: An activation function bends each output of a layer, which lets stacked layers describe curved relationships.

units.title: The multilayer perceptron (MLP)
units.summary: An MLP stacks linear layers with activation functions between them; it is the basic building block of neural networks.

units.title: Loss: one number for how wrong
units.summary: A loss function scores a model's predictions with one number that training tries to make small.

units.title: Gradient descent
units.summary: Gradient descent improves a model by repeatedly moving its weights a small step downhill on the loss.

units.title: AdamW: steps that adapt
units.summary: AdamW sizes each weight's step by how its gradients behaved recently, and gently shrinks weights toward zero.

units.title: Gradient clipping
units.summary: Gradient clipping caps the length of the gradient, so one unusual batch cannot throw the weights far off.

units.title: Learning-rate schedules: warm-up, decay
units.summary: A learning-rate schedule starts with small steps, grows them, then shrinks them as training settles.

units.title: Minibatches: a few examples per step
units.summary: Training estimates the loss from a small random batch of examples at each step, which is much faster than using them all.

units.title: Data loaders: preparing examples in parallel
units.summary: A data loader uses worker processes to prepare the next batches while the GPU trains on the current one.

units.title: Held-out data: the validation set
units.summary: A validation set is data the model never trains on, used to check that it has learned rather than memorized.

units.title: Overfitting: when a model fits the noise
units.summary: A model overfits when it fits the noise in its training examples and does worse on new ones; a penalty on large weights is a common remedy.

units.title: A moving average of the weights (EMA)
units.summary: An exponential moving average keeps a smoothed copy of the weights, which often gives better results than the latest weights.

units.title: Checkpoints: saving training to resume it
units.summary: A checkpoint saves the weights, the optimizer state and the step count, so training can stop and resume where it left off.

units.title: Mixed precision: 16-bit numbers (bf16)
units.summary: Mixed precision does most arithmetic in 16-bit numbers, which roughly halves the memory for activations and speeds up GPUs built for it, at a small cost in accuracy.

units.title: Training on several GPUs at once
units.summary: Data-parallel training gives each GPU its own share of a batch and averages their gradients before every step.

units.title: The training loop
units.summary: A training loop repeats one cycle (get a batch, compute the loss, take a step) and now and then evaluates and saves.

units.title: The sigmoid: from score to probability
units.summary: The sigmoid squashes any number into a probability between 0 and 1.

units.title: Binary cross-entropy: scoring yes-or-no guesses
units.summary: Binary cross-entropy charges a model heavily for confident wrong yes-or-no answers and little for confident right ones.

units.title: Softmax: probabilities over many choices
units.summary: Softmax turns a list of scores into probabilities that are all positive and add up to 1.

units.title: Cross-entropy: scoring a choice among many
units.summary: Cross-entropy is the loss for choosing one class among many: minus the logarithm of the probability given to the right one.

units.title: Top-K accuracy
units.summary: Top-K accuracy asks whether the right answer appears among the first K entries of a ranked list.

units.title: Embeddings: things as vectors
units.summary: An embedding represents each item, such as a word or a point, as a learned vector that a network can compute with.

units.title: Fourier features: positions as waves
units.summary: Fourier features describe a position by sine waves of several frequencies, which helps a network represent fine detail.

units.title: Attention: queries, keys, values
units.summary: Attention lets each token gather information from the others, weighting each by how well its key matches the token's query.

units.title: Cross-attention: reading from another set
units.summary: Cross-attention lets one set of tokens send its queries to a second set, such as the tokens of a condition.

units.title: Residual connections
units.summary: A residual connection adds a layer's input to its output, so a deep network learns small corrections and trains stably.

units.title: Layer normalization
units.summary: Layer normalization rescales each token's numbers to a standard mean and spread before the next layer uses them.

units.title: The transformer block
units.summary: A transformer block combines attention with an MLP, each wrapped in normalization and a residual connection.

units.title: PointNet pooling: one summary for a set
units.summary: PointNet applies the same MLP to every point and then takes a maximum, so the result does not depend on the points' order.

units.title: Generative models: making new examples
units.summary: A generative model learns what a collection of examples looks like, so it can produce new examples that fit in.

units.title: Conditional generation: generating from a hint
units.summary: A conditional generative model takes extra input, such as part of a shape, and generates outputs that fit it.

units.title: Shape completion: generating the missing part
units.summary: Shape completion generates the missing part of a partial shape, with the known part as the condition.

units.title: Velocity fields: an arrow at every point
units.summary: A velocity field gives every point of space, at every moment, an arrow saying where something there moves next.

units.title: Euler's method: small steps along a field
units.summary: Euler's method follows a velocity field by many small straight steps, each along the arrow where you stand.

units.title: Flow matching: turning noise into shapes
units.summary: Flow matching trains a network to predict the velocity that carries random noise along straight paths to real examples.

units.title: Time conditioning: telling a network the time
units.summary: A network that removes noise must know how noisy its input is; adaptive layer normalization (adaLN) feeds it the time.

units.title: Diffusion transformers (DiT)
units.summary: A diffusion transformer is a transformer, told the time in every block, that predicts how to move noisy tokens toward data.

units.title: Classifier-free guidance
units.summary: Classifier-free guidance strengthens a condition's effect by extrapolating from an unconditional prediction past a conditional one.

units.title: The diffusion noising process: from data to noise
units.summary: The standard noising process of a diffusion model shrinks an example and adds bell-curve noise over many steps, and any step can be reached in one jump.

units.title: The dot product: how much two vectors agree
units.summary: The dot product multiplies two vectors entry by entry and adds the results; it is large when they point the same way.

units.title: The chain rule: slopes of chained steps
units.summary: The chain rule finds the slope of a chain of steps by multiplying the slopes of the steps.

units.title: Broadcasting: arrays of different shapes
units.summary: Broadcasting lets NumPy combine arrays of different shapes by stretching each array along any axis that it lacks or that has length 1, without copying it.

units.title: Backpropagation: gradients by the chain rule
units.summary: Backpropagation computes every weight's gradient in one backward pass, applying the chain rule layer by layer.

units.title: Order doesn't matter: permutation invariance
units.summary: A permutation-invariant function gives the same answer however its inputs are ordered, which a model of point sets needs.

units.title: Floating-point numbers: rounding to the nearest stored value
units.summary: A computer stores a decimal number as a sign, a power of two and a fixed number of binary digits, so most numbers are rounded to the nearest stored value, and the gaps between stored values grow with their size.

units.title: Recursion: a function that calls itself
units.summary: A recursive function answers a small case directly and passes the rest of the problem to a new call of itself; the calls stop only if every chain of them reaches that small case.
